newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finland first to get over 30 pct cellular use.
newsitem.headline: Finland first to get over 30 pct cellular use.

text.p: Finland became the first country in the world with mobile phone penetration over 30 percent in mid-February, the ministry of transport and communications said in a statement received on Thursday.
Finland's five million population has 1.53 million mobile phones -- 910,000 digital and 620,000 analog -- it said.
The ministry said most phones were for private use.
A ministry official said February estimates showed Norway was second in the world with 29.2 percent, Sweden third with 28.5 percent and Australia fourth with an estimated 28 percent.

The ministry listed Iceland, Britain, Luxembourg and Italy as other European countries where cellular penetration is above 10 percent and said penetration in the U.S. was 17 percent and 15 percent in Japan.
Europe's largest mobile phone maker, Nokia Oy, is a Finnish company.
